html:
The Lheidli T'enneh are a group of the Dakelh, or Carrier, an Athabaskan people of central British Columbia. Their name means the people from where the two rivers flow together: their main village stood where the Nechako River joins the Fraser, the site of the city of Prince George.

They fished salmon on the rivers and hunted the forests and plateaus. In 1807 Simon Fraser of the North West Company built Fort George at the meeting of the rivers, and the post traded with them for most of a century. In 1913, as the railway and the new city came, the band was moved off its village to a reserve upriver. Neighbours include the Nadleh Whut'en and Stellat'en.
